title: Largest Rectangle in Histogram: The Widest Rooftop Banner
summary: An increasing stack of bars; each pop finds the widest rectangle at the popped bar's height.

analogy.scenario: Five buildings stand side by side with heights 2, 4, 3, 3, and 1. A rectangular banner must hang flat against them, no taller than the shortest building it covers. What's the biggest banner?

mapping.real: Buildings still able to extend a banner to the right
A shorter building cutting a banner off

takeaway.summary: Keep bars on a stack in increasing height. A shorter bar pops taller ones; each popped bar's rectangle spans from the bar below it on the stack to the new bar. Track the best area.
takeaway.timeComplexity: O(n): each bar is pushed and popped once
whenToUse: How far each item extends before something smaller stops it

scenes.narration: Five buildings stand in a row, heights 2, 4, 3, 3, and 1. A rectangular banner can't be taller than the shortest building it covers. What's the biggest banner?
scenes.caption: Buildings 2, 4, 3, 3, 1: the biggest flat banner?

scenes.narration: Trying every span of buildings and its shortest one is quadratic. Instead, keep buildings whose banners can still grow on a stack, heights rising.
scenes.caption: Trying every span of buildings is quadratic

scenes.narration: Heights 2 and 4 rise, so both go on the stack: their banners can still stretch to the right.
scenes.caption: 2, then 4: heights rise, so both wait

scenes.narration: A 3 is shorter than the 4 on top, so the 4's banner can't go further: pop it. It covers just its own building: 4 times 1 is 4.
scenes.caption: 3 cuts off the 4: its banner is 4 × 1 = 4

scenes.narration: The next building is also 3. It pops the first 3, whose banner spans two buildings: 3 times 2 is 6, a new best.
scenes.caption: The next 3 pops the first 3: 3 × 2 = 6

scenes.narration: The 1 cuts off the remaining 3. Its banner spans three buildings, from just past the 2: 3 times 3 is 9.
scenes.caption: Height 1 pops the last 3: 3 × 3 = 9

scenes.narration: The 1 also pops the 2, whose banner spans four buildings: 8, not better than 9.
scenes.caption: Then the 2 pops too: 2 × 4 = 8, not better

scenes.narration: A final height of 0 flushes the last building. Every building was popped once, and the biggest banner covers 9.
scenes.caption: Every building popped once: the biggest banner is 9

scenes.narration: Buildings are bars, and the rising stack tells each bar how far its rectangle reaches. Each bar is pushed and popped once: O(n).
scenes.caption: Buildings are bars; the rising stack finds each span
